sentences.text: This judgment shall dispose of Sessions Case No. 42 of 2023 arising out of FIR No. 118 dated 14.06.2022 registered at Police Station Civil Lines.
The accused Ramesh Kumar stands charged under Section 302 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code for the murder of Suresh Chand.
The question for determination is whether the prosecution has proved beyond reasonable doubt that the accused caused the death of the deceased in furtherance of common intention.
The case of the prosecution is that on the night of 13.06.2022 the deceased Suresh Chand was assaulted near the grain market.
PW-1 Karan Singh, the brother of the deceased, deposed that he saw the accused fleeing from the spot at about 11 PM.
PW-3 Dr. Meena Sharma, who conducted the post-mortem, opined that death was caused by two incised wounds on the chest inflicted by a sharp-edged weapon.
PW-5 the Investigating Officer stated that despite extensive search, no weapon was recovered from the accused or at his instance.
The Test Identification Parade could not be conducted as the accused was already known to PW-1.
PW-7 Mohan Lal, an independent witness, stated that the street light near the grain market was not functional on the night of occurrence.
The accused in his statement under Section 313 CrPC denied the allegations and stated that he was at his village Dhablan on the night of the occurrence.
DW-1 Gurmeet Singh supported the plea of alibi and stated that the accused attended a wedding at Dhablan on the night of 13.06.2022.
Learned counsel for the accused argued that the identification by PW-1 in darkness is wholly unreliable and that the alibi stands unrebutted.
The learned Public Prosecutor argued that PW-1 knew the accused for years and could identify him even in poor light.
I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record carefully.
The testimony of PW-1 is consistent and he had sufficient opportunity to observe the accused whom he knew previously.
The medical evidence of PW-3 corroborates the ocular account regarding the nature of injuries.
It is true that no weapon was recovered, but non-recovery of the weapon is not fatal to the prosecution case when the ocular evidence is trustworthy.
The plea of alibi set up by the accused is not established, as DW-1 is a close relative and no independent record of the wedding was produced.
The presence of the accused at the spot at 11 PM stands proved through the testimony of PW-1.
In view of the above discussion, the prosecution has proved its case beyond reasonable doubt.
The accused Ramesh Kumar is accordingly convicted under Section 302 read with Section 34 IPC and sentenced to imprisonment for life and a fine of Rs. 10,000.
